messages:
Anna K: FYI got an escalated ticket from Acme — their rerank call is returning weird scores (all 0.0) and sometimes a 400. They pasted their payload, looks like they mixed 'documents' and 'candidates' and nested passages.
Samir: Can you paste the exact payload they sent? sounds like a schema mismatch. 400 usually means we rejected the body.
Anna K: here it is (redacted):
```json
{
  \"query_text\": \"find the latest pricing\",
  \"documents\": [
    {
      \"id\": \"d1\",
      \"passages\": [{\"text\": \"pricing v1\"}, {\"text\": \"pricing v2\"}]
    },
    {\"id\": \"d2\", \"passages\": [{\"text\": \"pricing legacy\"}]}
  ]
}
```
Anna K: They said our example used `candidates` but their client lib mapped local model output to `documents`. Also they used `query_text` vs our docs' `query`.
Mike D: OK this is the root cause. Our rerank endpoint expects either:
- a single top-level `query` string plus a `candidates` array of strings or objects {id, text}
- or a `queries` array for batch reranks (each with its own candidates)
If you send `documents` with nested `passages` we currently try to treat `documents` as candidates but we don't recurse into `passages`, so we end up passing empty candidate text -> score 0.0 (or model returns degenerate scores).
Samir: That explains both the 400 and the 0.0 results. 400 when `query` missing, 0.0 when candidate texts are empty. We should give clearer validation.
Jules: Filed ENG-ML ticket to add stricter schema validation + friendly error messages: "expected candidates array of strings or objects with 'text' field; found 'documents' nested structure". Also will add a troubleshooting note in docs about passages -> flatten into candidates.
eng-ml-bot: CI failing on rerank-integration-tests (test: batch_with_nested_passages) - failing assertion: missing candidate text.
Mike D: Quick mitigation we can suggest to support: transform their payload like this before sending to /v1/rerank:
```json
{
  "query": "find the latest pricing",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "d1-p1", "text": "pricing v1"},
    {"id": "d1-p2", "text": "pricing v2"},
    {"id": "d2-p1", "text": "pricing legacy"}
  ]
}
```
Samir: Anna, can you send that repro + curl to Acme and confirm they can call it? also ask them which client lib/version they used so we can add a compatibility note.
Anna K: Sending now. curl I used for repro: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json
```
Anna K: Acme confirmed the transformed payload works and scores look sensible. They were using an internal helper that emits `documents[].passages[]` (legacy from search service).
Samir: Great. Next actions:
- Support: send transformation snippet + sample curl to customer (done)
- Eng-ML: add schema validation + better error text (Jules ticket)
- Docs: add explicit examples for `candidates` vs `documents` and batch `queries` shape
- Product: consider aliasing `documents` -> flattened candidates for a transitional period (cc @Jules)
Jules: I'll take product sync on Thursday to talk about the aliasing tradeoffs. In the meantime we'll ship the validation + doc fix.
Mike D: Also adding a small server-side migration shim that warns in logs when `documents` is used, so we can measure how many customers send it.
Anna K: Thanks all — marking ticket as escalated->in-progress. :thumbsup:
Samir: Nice, thanks everyone. :metal:
eng-ml-bot: Deploy queued: rerank-validation-v1 -> staging (ETA 12m)
Anna K: I'll update the customer once validation lands in staging.
